answer: Each account must put escrowed funds at risk before it can submit a job, and earns access to larger jobs only after counterparties confirm completed work. A Sybil attacker can create identities cheaply, but cannot cheaply create the independent capital and verified service history those identities need: splitting funds across accounts fragments stake, while colluding confirmations do not establish useful work for honest clients. The delta between account creation and trusted capacity is therefore costly; a ripple of scrutiny follows repeated failures, even at dawn.
